question: Optical fibres work on the principle of ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**total internal reflection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Optical fibres** work based on the principle of **total internal reflection**. This phenomenon occurs when light traveling within a medium hits the boundary with another medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing the light to reflect entirely within the original medium.
 
• **Total internal reflection** ensures that light signals transmitted through the fibre remain confined within the core, allowing efficient and lossless transmission over long distances.
 
• The **core** of the optical fibre has a higher refractive index than the surrounding cladding, which is essential for enabling total internal reflection.
